the_ruling_verbatim.note: Akien's words, in order, correcting a line CC had just written into cairn/tools/feedback/intention+why.json. CC's contributions are kept out of this field on purpose.
the_ruling_verbatim.1_the_correction: "node_class": "tool — a complete primitive with USERS, not an owner (Law 6). It holds no state; charters are read on demand and nothing is remembered between calls. ...", NOT ENTIERLY CORRECT: YOU AND I EXPLICITLY TALKED ABOUT TOOLS AND MACHINES AND HOW THEIR STATE WOULD BE MANAGED: If a starting state is needed, it's in the code. ongoing state is in the runtime folder. ~/.cairn/devices/<device class>/<device name/num>/tools/<tool class>/<tool name/num>/whatever data. So even completely no LLM can have instance or class level memories (i'm using this word here to mean all kinds of state and history data that might go there)
the_ruling_verbatim.2_the_why: right because each instance of the tool or machine can have it's own data
the_ruling_verbatim.4_the_hidden_capability_called_out: sorry to interrupt but there's a hidden capability in there that i should actually call out explicitly so there's no ambiguity later: The path above allows a class of tools within a given machine or device to have class shared files. there's a folder that holds all the instances within that parent. i don't have a use for it in my head. but that use is not excluded.

now_the_spec_says.a_tool_remembers: A TOOL — AND A MACHINE — CAN CARRY STATE AND HISTORY, WITH NO LLM ANYWHERE NEAR IT. The split is by ADDRESS, not by capability: if a STARTING state is needed it ships in the CODE, in class-space; ONGOING state berths in the runtime tree at ~/.cairn/devices/<device class>/<device name|num>/tools/<tool class>/<tool name|num>/ , and machines get a folder right alongside tools. 'Memory' here is Akien's own scoping of the word: ALL KINDS of state and history data that might go there, not a learned model.
now_the_spec_says.the_reason_and_it_is_the_operative_claus: 'each instance of the tool or machine can have it's own data'. The instance segment is what the address BUYS — two instances of the same tool class, held by the same device instance, do not share a drawer unless something puts a file one rung up.
now_the_spec_says.the_class_shared_folder_NEW: EVERY CLASS SEGMENT IN THAT PATH IS A REAL FOLDER, AND A FOLDER CAN HOLD FILES. tools/<tool class>/ is the folder that holds all instances of that tool class within that one holder, so it can also hold files SHARED by them. Akien called this out explicitly to remove later ambiguity, and bounded it in the same breath: 'i don't have a use for it in my head. but that use is not excluded.' So it is an AFFORDANCE OF THE SHAPE, deliberately NOT BUILT and NOT TICKETED — recorded so that a later reader finds it already permitted rather than re-deriving it, and so that nobody builds a mechanism for a use nobody has named. CC's observation, offered as such and not as Akien's word: the same physics runs at EVERY class rung of the path — devices/<device class>/ holds all instances of the device class, machines/<machine class>/ all instances of the machine class — because the segment is a directory in each case. Nothing turns on this today; it is written down so the tool rung is not later read as a special case.
now_the_spec_says.the_scope_of_class_shared: HOLDER-SCOPED, NOT GLOBAL. tools/<tool class>/ sits UNDER one device instance, so a file there is shared by that class's instances WITHIN THAT HOLDER and by nothing else. There is no cross-device drawer for a tool class in this shape, and the absence is the point: a tool's definition and defaults are the only thing that berths once, in class-space, in git.
now_the_spec_says.what_this_does_to_law_6: NOTHING — but it kills the REASONING that had been carrying it. Law 6 stands: a tool has USERS, not an owner. What is now wrong is the derivation 'a tool holds no state, THEREFORE it has nothing to gate'. The true version is narrower by one word: a tool has no state OF ITS OWN, because its ongoing state hangs off the HOLDER that assembled it, and is therefore the holder's to own and gate. The test survives in refined form: anything called a tool that must gate writes AT ITS OWN ADDRESS is a machine.

what_dies: 'A tool holds no state' as a PROPERTY OF TOOLHOOD. It is false. What is true is per-build and per-tool — 'TODAY this tool persists nothing' — and it is a fact about that build, never a fact about tools.

The derivation in ruling 2026-08-13-tools-have-users-not-owners, now_the_spec_says: 'Ownership gates writes to state and a tool holds none, so there is nothing to gate — and anything called a tool that needs an owner holds state and is not one.' THE RULING ITSELF STANDS (a tool has users, not an owner); its stated reason is superseded by this one. That record is append-only and is NOT edited (Law 7); this ruling is the reader's next stop from it.
CC's line in cairn/tools/feedback/intention+why.json that occasioned the correction — the one that read 'It holds no state; charters are read on demand and nothing is remembered between calls.'
what_conforms: decision 2026-08-12-tools-machines-devices-instances, field 4_INSTANCE_DATA_FOR_HELD_PARTS: 'a device may have many machines and tools, and those may need instance data. yesterday we talked about .cairn/devices/device/instance/tools/name/whatever data --- as the way to manage that. machines can have a folder right along side tools'. THIS RULING IS NOT NEW GROUND — it is the same spec, said twice, and the second saying was needed because CC had written the contradiction into four charters and two docstrings in between. That is the measurement of the failure, not a defence of it.

CLAUDE.md's own layout paragraph: 'a tool's definition and defaults berth once in tools/, and everything beyond the defaults hangs off the holder that assembled it' — already correct, and already sitting in the same file as the sentence it contradicts.
decision 2026-08-12, the_probe_split_NEW: a probe's DEFINITION lives in the code and its RUNTIME DATA in the .cairn tree. The same seam, one rung down.
The naming-over-numbering ratification (Akien, 2026-08-11: 'gates with names instead of numbers: perfect') — the <tool name|num> segment is named wherever a name exists.

measured_by_cc_2026_08_14.note: CC's measurements, labelled as CC's. Nothing here is Akien's word.
measured_by_cc_2026_08_14.how_far_the_wrong_claim_had_spread: grep for the property-of-toolhood claim across cairn/ found it live at eight sites, authored by CC: cairn/tools/gate/intention+why.json:8 and :29 (the :29 one is the worst — it makes Law 6 TRACE TO statelessness), cairn/tools/determinism/intention+why.json:8 and :23, cairn/tools/import_sieve/intention+why.json:8, cairn/tools/gate/gate.py:63, cairn/tools/chain/grammar.py:13, and CLAUDE.md's Law 6 itself.
measured_by_cc_2026_08_14.not_touched_and_why: cairn/tools/base/probe.py, cairn/tools/base/shim.py and cairn/devices/web_server/intention+why.json also say 'holds no state', and are LEFT INTACT: a Probe is a frozen dataclass and that is a real design fact about probes, and the web_server line is about a presentation surface owning no content state, which is a different claim entirely. The sweep is of a wrong DERIVATION, not of a string.
measured_by_cc_2026_08_14.how_it_propagated: CC wrote the feedback tool's node_class line by copying gate's. A wrong sentence in a charter is not inert — it is the pattern the next charter is written from, which is what makes 'solidify the layer below' load-bearing rather than tidy.

not_built_not_ticketed: The class-shared folder. Permitted by the shape, no use named, no mechanism, no placeholder. Akien: 'i don't have a use for it in my head. but that use is not excluded.'
Any instance-path resolver. decision 2026-08-12 already names it as NOT BUILT (six call sites, five hardcoding the 0) and that debt is unchanged by this ruling — it is not re-filed here.
